title: What happens when you click Login? (in the car)
note: Sample content, made up for the first end-to-end test. Characters, car and voices are placeholders.

intro.action: human walks out of the building door and stops at the curb
message typed on the phone screen
the car pulls up to the curb and stops in front of the human

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: Yeah. Hey, quick question while we drive. What actually happens when I click Login?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: Ooh, good one. Picture your browser handing a note to the server. Your email, and your password.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: Wait, it just sends my password?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: Over an encrypted connection, yes. And the server never stores it. Only a scrambled fingerprint, called a hash.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: So how does it check it's me?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: It scrambles what you typed and compares the fingerprints. A match, and you're in. Then it hands you a token, like a signed pass.

lines.speaker: human
lines.text: And I just show that pass every time?

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: Every request. That's all being logged in is. Proof you keep showing.

lines.speaker: claude
lines.text: Most things are, once you see them move. Next stop: home.

cutRule: interior: while CLAUDE speaks use CAM_HUMAN_POV (we see Claude), while the HUMAN speaks use CAM_CLAUDE_POV (we see the human in the mirror); cut on the first word, hold at least 1.2 s; the 0.35 s gap stays on the previous shot
